rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The preceding argument concludes that the material in question would count as purification; this is Abu Hanifa’s doctrine.
rows.anchor: لكان ذلك طهوره

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Some interpreters take min in the parallel tayammum wording as marking the starting point rather than a portion.
rows.anchor: قالوا إن ( من ) لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author accepts the objection that this analysis is strained: Arabic ordinarily hears a partitive in wiping with some oil, water, or soil, and yielding to truth is better than disputation.
rows.anchor: ولا يفهم أحد من العرب من قول القائل مسحت برأسه من الدهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God forgiving and pardoning alludes to legal license and ease: one who habitually forgives prefers ease rather than difficulty.
rows.anchor: كناية عن الترخيص والتيسير لأن من كانت عادته أن يعفو عن الخطائين

words: وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰٓ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum applies to anyone obligated to purify who lacks water, including those fearing an enemy or beast, lacking a drawing tool, or stranded where no water is available.
rows.anchor: ثم عم كل من وجب عليه التطهر وأعوزه الماء لخوف عدو أو سبع

words: وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰٓ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick and travelers are named first because illness and travel are frequent and therefore have the strongest initial claim to an explanation of the license.
rows.anchor: فخص أول من بينهم مرضاهم وسفرهم لأنهم متقدمون في استحقاق بيان الرخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has min ghayṭ, described as a lightened form of ghāʾiṭ; ghayṭ means the same as ghāʾiṭ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( من غيط ) قيل هو تخفيف غيط

none: Verse marker only; no commentary is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who praise themselves are Jews and Christians, who claimed to be God’s children and beloved and said only Jews or Christians would enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: اليهود والنصارى قالوا نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed report says Jewish men brought their children to the Prophet, who said the children had no sin; they claimed their own daytime sins were erased at night and nighttime sins by day, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: بأطفالهم فقالوا هل على هؤلاء ذنب قال ( لا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning includes anyone who declares their own deeds, obedience, piety, or nearness to God pure and superior.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيها كل من زكى نفسه ووصفها بزكاء العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement that he was trustworthy in heaven and earth came after hypocrites demanded fair division, refuting their accusation that he acted unlike God’s description of him.
rows.anchor: إنما قال ذلك حين قال له المنافقون اعدل في القسمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God’s purification counts, since He knows who deserves it; He purifies approved servants whom He recognizes as pure and describes accordingly.
rows.anchor: اعلام بأن تزكية الله هي التي يعتد بها لا تزكية غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purifies servants He approves, recognizing their purity and describing them by it.
rows.anchor: يزكي المرتضين من عباده الذين عرف منهم الزكاء فوصفهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible sense is that self-praisers receive the full measure of punishment they deserve for praising themselves.
rows.anchor: أي الذين يزكون أنفسهم يعاقبون على تزكيتهم أنفسهم حق جزائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, those whom God purifies receive the full reward for their purity, with none of it diminished.
rows.anchor: أو من يشاء يثابون على زكائهم ولا ينقص من ثوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This echoes the prohibition on self-praise because God knows best who is pious.
rows.anchor: فلا تزكوا أنفسكم هو أعلم بمن اتقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their assertion that they are pure before God is an instance of fabricating a lie against Him.
rows.anchor: في زعمهم أنهم عند الله أزكياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim of purity alone suffices as an evident sin among all their other sins.
rows.anchor: في زعمهم أنهم عند الله أزكياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means that God exchanged other skins for them.
rows.anchor: أبدلناهم إياها فإن قلت كيف نعذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: New skins may be punished because punishment concerns the sensitive whole that sinned, not the skin in isolation.
rows.anchor: العذاب للجملة الحساسة وهي التي عصت لا للجلد

rows.speaker: فضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl explains the renewal as making what has been cooked or scorched unscorched again.
rows.anchor: وعن فضيل يجعل النضيج غير نضيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says their skins are replaced seven times each day; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( 285 ) ( تبدل جلودهم كل يوم سبع مرات )

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the skins are replaced seventy times, becoming white like sheets of paper.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : سبعين مرة يبدلون جلودا بيضاء كالقراطيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose clause means their experience of punishment continues without interruption, as in a wish that someone’s strength endure and increase.
rows.anchor: ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع . كقولك للعزيز : أعزك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty because nothing He wills against the criminals can stop Him.
rows.anchor: لا يمتنع عليه شيء مما يريده بالمجرمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is wise because He punishes only with justice those who deserve punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يعذب إلا بعدل من يستحقه

none: Opening marker only; no commentary is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is emphatic because the sentence opens with innamā.
rows.anchor: منها تصدير الجملة بإنما ومنها أنه قرنهما بعبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine and gambling are paired with idol worship to intensify their prohibition.
rows.anchor: ومنها أنه قرنهما بعبادة الأصنام ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet likens a wine drinker to an idol worshipper; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام 365 ( شارب الخمر كعابد الوثن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The association with idols echoes the command to avoid the filth of idols.
rows.anchor: فاجتنبوا الرجس من الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them satanic works emphasizes the prohibition because Satan produces nothing but sheer evil.
rows.anchor: ومنها أنه جعلهما من عمل الشيطان والشيطان لا يأتي منه إلا الشر البحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct command to avoid them is another emphasis of the prohibition.
rows.anchor: ومنها أنه أمر بالاجتناب ومنها أنه جعل الاجتناب من الفلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since avoidance is identified with success, committing these acts entails failure and ruin.
rows.anchor: إذا كان الاجتناب فلاحا كان الارتكاب خيبة ومحقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their harms include hostility and hatred among drinkers and gamblers, diversion from remembering God, and neglect of prayer times.
rows.anchor: وقوع التعادي والتباغض من أصحاب الخمر والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is among the most forceful prohibitions: after all deterrents are recited, it asks whether they will stop or persist as if never admonished.
rows.anchor: من أبلغ ما ينهى عنه كأنه قيل قد تلي عليكم ما فيهما من أنواع الصوارف والموانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to an omitted noun such as wine and gambling, their consumption or practice, or something similar.
rows.anchor: إلى المضاف المحذوف كأنه قيل إنما شأن الخمر والميسر أو تعاطيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols and divining arrows are grouped with wine and gambling to stress that all are pre-Islamic practices of polytheists and must be avoided.
rows.anchor: وذكر الأنصاب والأزلام لتأكيد تحريم الخمر والميسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After grouping all four practices, the verse singles out wine and gambling to show they are its central targets.
rows.anchor: ثم أفردهما بالذكر ليرى أن المقصود بالذكر الخمر والميسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out from remembrance as though the wording meant especially prayer.
rows.anchor: اختصاص للصلاة من بين الذكر كأنه قيل وعن الصلاة خصوصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment points to the continuation in al-Māʾida 5:92.
rows.anchor: المائدة 92

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people ridiculing and attacking God’s verses were Quraysh doing so in their meeting places.
rows.anchor: وكانت قريش في أنديتهم يفعلون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turn away means do not sit with them and leave their gathering.
rows.anchor: فلا تجالسهم وقم عنهم { حتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once they move to a different topic, sitting with them is permissible.
rows.anchor: فلا بأس أن تجالسهم حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean Satan distracts you by whispering until you forget the prohibition on sitting with them.
rows.anchor: وإن شغلك بوسوسته حتى تنسى النهي عن مجالستهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, before the prohibition, Satan may make you forget that reason itself condemns sitting with mockers; the reminder means God warned you of its ugliness.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الشيطان ينسينك قبل النهي قبح مجالسة

words: وَمَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mindful bear none of the mockers’ sins or reckoning, but must remind them by leaving, showing disapproval, and admonishing them.
rows.anchor: وما يلزم المتقين الذين يجالسونهم شيء مما يحاسبون عليه من ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder may make the mockers stop out of embarrassment or reluctance to upset the believers.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يجتنبون الخوض حياء أو كراهة لمساءتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun can refer to the mindful themselves: they remind the mockers to remain firm and increase in piety.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير للذين يتقون

rows.speaker: المسلمون
rows.claim: Muslims said that leaving every time the Qur’an was mocked would make it impossible to sit in the Sacred Mosque or circumambulate; a concession was then given.
rows.anchor: المسلمين قالوا : لئن كنا نقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikrā can be accusative as an emphatic verbal noun for reminding them, or nominative as a reminder incumbent on them; it cannot coordinate with min shay because min ḥisābihim blocks that parsing.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون نصبا على : ولكن يذكرونهم ذكرى

none: Continuation marker only; no commentary is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come alone, separated from wealth, children, worldly things they preferred, and idols they claimed were intercessors and partners of God.
rows.anchor: منفردين عن أموالكم وأولادكم وما حرصتم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrive in the original condition of solitude in which they were born.
rows.anchor: على الهيئة التي ولدتم عليها في الانفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly gifts they leave behind did not benefit them; they carried away nothing small and sent nothing ahead for themselves.
rows.anchor: لم ينفعكم ولم تحتملوا منه نقيرا ولا قدمتموه لأنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed partners are idols: by naming and worshipping them as gods, people made them partners in their own enslavement to God.
rows.anchor: حين دعوهم آلهة وعبدوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read furādā with tanwīn, furād, or furdā, by analogy with sukārā.
rows.anchor: فراد ، مثل ثلاث . وفردى ، نحو سكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is accusative as an adjective of the verbal noun implied by jīʾtum: your coming is like the way We first created you.
rows.anchor: في محل النصب صفة لمصدر جئتمونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing treats separation as a verbal noun made the subject: separation occurred between you, like saying that a joining was brought about.
rows.anchor: وقع التقطع بينكم ، كما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the raised reading, the verb is assigned to the adverbial phrase, like saying that fighting occurred behind or before you.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع فقد أسند الفعل إلى الظرف كما تقول قوتل خلفكم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah’s reading has mā as the subject: la-qad taqaṭṭaʿa mā baynakum.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله : ( لقد تقطع ما بينكم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God splits grain and pits by bringing forth the growing plant and tree.
rows.anchor: { فالق الحب والنوى } بالنبات والشجر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means the two clefts in a date pit and a wheat grain.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : أراد الشقين الذين في النواة والحنطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living things from dead things include animals and growing things produced from semen, eggs, grain, and pits.
rows.anchor: أي الحيوان ، والنامي من النطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The converse is the production of lifeless seed, grain, and pits from animals and growing things.
rows.anchor: هذه الأشياء الميتة من الحيوان والنامي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukh rij is coordinated with fāliq, not the finite verb; the clause about bringing living from dead explains splitting, since growing plants count as living.
rows.anchor: عطفه على فالق الحب والنوى ، لا على الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this sign of growth with the signs of God’s mercy in the revival of the earth.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله : { فانظر إلىءاثار رحمة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life-giver and death-causer is God, alone deserving lordship.
rows.anchor: هو الله الذي تحق له الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks how people can turn away from God and devotion to Him toward another.
rows.anchor: فكيف تصرفون عنه وعن توليه إلى غيره

none: Continuation marker only; no commentary is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-iṣbāḥ is a verbal noun used as a name for dawn; with the opening hamza vowel it is also read as a plural meaning mornings.
rows.anchor: الإصباح } مصدر سمي به الصبح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads iṣbāḥ with a fatḥa on the hamza as a plural of ṣubḥ; the cited line uses the word for morning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بفتح الهمزة جمع صبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn forms with kasra and fatḥa can be verbal nouns; the corresponding evening and morning forms can also be plurals.
rows.anchor: بالكسر والفتح مصدرين ، وجمع مساء وصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Splitting dawn can mean splitting late-night darkness bordering morning, or splitting dawn itself as its column of light emerges.
rows.anchor: وهي الغبش في آخر الليل ، ومنقضاه الذي يلي الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is called falaq in the sense of something split open; Arabs describe its column as cleft and split.
rows.anchor: وانصدع الفجر . وسموا الفجر فلقا بمعنى مفلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭāʾī’s line says blue dawn appears before its white, witnessing the light’s gradual emergence.
rows.anchor: وأزرق الفجر يبدو قبل أبيضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has fāliq al-iṣbāḥ and jāʿil al-layl in the accusative as praise; al-Nakhaʿī reads falaq al-iṣbāḥ and jaʿala al-layl.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( فالق الإصباح ، وجاعل الليل سكنا ) بالنصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan is what gives a person comfort, such as a spouse or beloved; fire is also called sakan because people enjoy its company.
rows.anchor: السكن : ما يسكن إليه الرجل ويطمئن استئناسا به واسترواحا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night calms those exhausted by daytime with rest and renewal; alternatively, it is the time in which people dwell.
rows.anchor: والليل يطمئن إليه التعب بالنهار لاستراحته فيه وجمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon are read in the accusative, genitive, or nominative; the accusative supplies a verb, the genitive coordinates with night, and the nominative begins a clause with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: فالنصب على إضمار فعل دل عليه جاعل الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night can serve as an object for coordination because the participle’s genitive construction denotes an ongoing act, not a past action.
rows.anchor: ما هو معنى المضي ، وإنما هو دال على جعل مستمر في الأزمنة المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the sun and moon ḥusbān means setting them to a calculated course by which people reckon time; ḥusbān is a verbal noun with two vocalizations.
rows.anchor: جعلهما على حسبان ، لأن حساب الأوقات يعلم بدورهما وسيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to their calculated movement; the Mighty subdues them, and the Knowing governs their courses.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى جعلهما حسبانا ، أي ذلك التسيير بالحساب المعلوم

none: Quoted verse only; no commentary is present.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the qāf, mustawdaʿ is a place noun or verbal noun; with kasra, mustaqirr is active and mustawdaʿ passive.
rows.anchor: من فتح قاف المستقر ، كان المستودع اسم مكان مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms may mean a fixed place in the womb and a deposit in the loins, above and beneath the earth, or fixed and deposited people among you.
rows.anchor: فلكم مستقر في الرحم . ومستودع في الصلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development from one soul is subtler and demands closer thought than the stars, so this verse says people who reflect while the preceding one says those who know.
rows.anchor: كان إنشاء الإنس من نفس واحدة وتصريفهم بين أحوال مختلفة ألطف وأدق صنعة وتدبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water produces every kind of growing thing: the cause is one, while the resulting species are varied.
rows.anchor: نبت كل صنف من أصناف النامي ، يعني أن السبب واحد وهو الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaḍir is a tender green shoot branching from the plant base grown from the seed; the word has singular and collective forms.
rows.anchor: شيئا غضا أخضر . يقال خضر وخضر ، كأعور وعور ، وهو ما تشعب من أصل النبات الخارج من الحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clustered grain produced from the green shoot is the ear of grain.
rows.anchor: من الخضر { حبا متراكبا } وهو السنبل

words: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinwān can be a subject with min al-nakhl its predicate and min ṭalʿihā an apposition; alternatively, an omitted predicate is supplied from the earlier verb.
rows.anchor: و { قنوان } رفع الابتداء . و { من * النخل } خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the reading yakhruju, qinwān coordinates with ḥabb rather than serving as a new subject.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ يخرج منه حب متراكب ، كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qinwān is the plural of qinw, like ṣinw and ṣinwān; its qāf is read with ḍamma or fatḥa, the latter as a collective noun.
rows.anchor: والقنوان : جمع قنو ، ونظيره : صنو وصنوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearby clusters are easy to pick; even a short palm bears fruit without waiting to grow tall.
rows.anchor: سهلة المجتنى معرضة للقاطف ، كالشيء الداني القريب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the date clusters are close to one another.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : دانية قريب بعضها من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Near clusters are mentioned while distant ones are omitted because the blessing is clearer in the near ones, which imply the distant ones; the author compares the mention of protection from heat.
rows.anchor: ذكر القريبة وترك ذكر البعيدة : لأن النعمة فيها أظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens of grapes can be an additional item alongside palms or coordinated with qinwān as another product.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان ، أحدهما : أن يراد : وثم جنات من أعناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative can coordinate these products with plants of every kind; the author prefers parsing them as a specification because these fruits deserve special mention.
rows.anchor: والأحسن أن ينتصبا على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishtabaha and tashābaha often share a meaning; the variant describes olives and pomegranates as alike and unlike.
rows.anchor: يقال اشتبه الشيئان وتشابها ، كقولك استويا وتساويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads mutashābihan wa-ghayra mutashābih, with both fruits understood as alike and unlike.
rows.anchor: وتقديره : والزيتون متشابها وغير متشابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun can refer to the act introduced by the prohibition, to the relative food, or to food lacking God’s name as itself sinful.
rows.anchor: الضمير راجع إلى مصدر الفعل الذي دخل عليه حرف النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some jurists allow food lacking God’s name when the omission was accidental or intentional; they interpret the passage as concerning carrion or food dedicated to another than God.
rows.anchor: قد ذهب جماعة من المجتهدين إلى جواز أكل ما لم يذكر اسم الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative interpretation takes the prohibited food as carrion, or food over which another than God was invoked.
rows.anchor: كقوله : { أو فسقا أهل لغير الله به }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whisperers are devils and their allies are polytheists, whom they incite to argue against eating what God has killed.
rows.anchor: ليسوسون { إلى أوليائهم } من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following anyone besides God in religious practice makes a person a polytheist.
rows.anchor: لأن من اتبع غير الله تعالى في دينه فقد أشرك به

words: وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A discerning believer should avoid such food in every case because the verse’s wording is strongly prohibitive.
rows.anchor: ومن حق ذي البصيرة في دينه أن لا يأكل

words: وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa permits eating it when the omission was accidental, but not when deliberate.
rows.anchor: وإن كان أبو حنيفة رحمة الله مرخصا في النسيان دون العمد

words: وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi permit eating it whether the omission was accidental or deliberate.
rows.anchor: ومالك والشافعي رحمهما الله فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person, raised from misguidance and given certainty to distinguish truth from falsehood, resembles someone revived and given light to move among people and discern them; the misguided remain lost in darkness.
rows.anchor: مثل الذي هداه الله بعد الضلالة ومنحه التوفيق لليقين

words: كَمَن مَّثَلُهُۥ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِّنْهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means someone whose description is that he is in darkness and cannot leave it.
rows.anchor: هو في الظلمات ليس بخارج منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares this construction to the description of Paradise as having rivers: the following clause supplies the likeness’s attribute.
rows.anchor: أي صفتها هذه ، وهي قوله : { فيها أنهار }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeds may have been made attractive to disbelievers by Satan.
rows.anchor: أي زينه الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God made their deeds attractive, as in the verse saying that We adorned their deeds.
rows.anchor: أو الله عز وعلا على قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Makkah’s chiefs were left to scheme, so are the greatest criminals in each town; they are singled out because they lead people into error and plot against them.
rows.anchor: يعني : وكما جعلنا في مكة صناديدها ليمكروا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads akbar mujrimihā, meaning the biggest criminals of each town.
rows.anchor: هم أكبر قومهم ، وأكابر قومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plotting only harms themselves because its consequences rebound on them; the statement consoles the Prophet and promises victory.
rows.anchor: لأن مكرهم يحيق بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement consoles the Prophet and promises in advance that he will prevail over them.
rows.anchor: وهذه تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتقديم موعد بالنصرة عليهم

rows.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
rows.claim: Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra claimed he deserved prophethood more because he was older and wealthier than the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الوليد بن المغيرة قال : لو كانت النبوة حقا

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abū Jahl said his clan had matched Banū ʿAbd Manāf in honor but would not accept their prophet unless they too received revelation.
rows.anchor: أن أبا جهل قال : زاحمنا بني عبد مناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s willing to guide means granting gracious favor; He wills that favor only for someone fit to receive it.
rows.anchor: أن يلطف به ولا يريد أن يلطف إلا بمن له لطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening the breast means granting favor until the person desires Islam, feels at ease with it, and loves entering it.
rows.anchor: يلطف به حتى يرغب في الإسلام وتسكن إليه نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Willing to lead astray means withholding favor, abandoning the person, and leaving him to himself.
rows.anchor: أن يخذله ويخليه وشأنه ، وهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A constricted breast results from withholding divine favors until the heart hardens, recoils from truth, and shuts against faith.
rows.anchor: وينبو عن قبول الحق وينسد فلا يدخله الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍayyiqan is read with light or doubled yāʾ; ḥarajan with kasra or fatḥa, the latter a verbal noun used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: بالكسر ، حرجا بالفتح وصفا بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image compares the constricted person to someone undertaking an impossible ascent beyond human capacity.
rows.anchor: كأنما يزاول أمرا غير ممكن . لأن صعود السماء مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has readings yaṣʿadu, yataṣaʿʿadu, and yuṣāʿidu; Abdullah reads yataṣaʿʿadu, and the author explains their derivations.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله : ( يتصعد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs can mean abandonment and deprivation of divine success, the opposite of the purity associated with guidance.
rows.anchor: يعني الخذلان ومنع التوفيق ، وصفه بنقيض ما يوصف به التوفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, rijs is the act leading to impurity, namely punishment, from a root meaning agitation.
rows.anchor: أو أراد الفعل المؤدي إلى الرجس وهو العذاب من الارتجاس وهو الاضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the way established by divine wisdom in granting or withholding guidance; straight means just and consistent.
rows.anchor: وهذا طريقه الذي اقتضته الحكمة وعادته في التوفيق والخذلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dār al-salām is either God’s house, honored by attribution to Him, or a house safe from every harm and distress.
rows.anchor: دار الله ، يعني الجنة أضافها إلى نفسه تعظيما لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is secured by God’s guarantee or is a reserve whose full reality they do not know, like hidden comforts.
rows.anchor: في ضمانه كما تقول لفلان عندي حق لا ينسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wali may mean their patron and beloved, or their helper against enemies.
rows.anchor: مواليهم ومحبهم أو ناصرهم على أعدائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean because of their deeds, or that God takes charge of them by repaying them for their deeds.
rows.anchor: بسبب أعمالهم ، أو متوليهم بجزاه ما كانوا يعملون
